battle.name: 孟海公起義
battle.brief: 大業九年（613），隋煬帝第二次征高句麗、括戶加派之際，濟北郡人孟海公聚眾起兵，自號「黑社帥」，眾至數萬，轉掠齊州、濟北縣邑，與竇建德、張金稱等河北起義遙相呼應，終為郡兵與追討騎兵所破。卡面羅馬方陣盾非此役器物；對應的是隋軍長槊結陣之盾與起義軍自備的柴刀竹槊。

kit.name: 羅馬方陣盾
kit.history: 凸面的長方盾。羅馬的防線靠盾緣咬住盾緣，不是靠盾牌多厚。

countries: 交戰雙方是隋朝在山東濟北郡一線的國家機器一方，和由孟海公以「黑社帥」號召起來的鄉里武裝一方。隋朝這一邊，真正能作戰的部隊遠在北方：第二次征高句麗抽走了京師宿衛、關右精兵與沿江的漕運人力，留守中州的只有各州郡就地抽丁編成的郡兵、縣兵，戰時執矛披甲、列柵守城，戰罷歸農；能追討的只有少數自前線調回或臨時募得的精騎，由經驗宿將率領，奉詔逐縣搜捕。濟北郡治所在陽谷，屬齊州管轄，郡兵平時的任務是城守、緝拿逃戶、督修堤防，兵源來自編戶，器械多為鄉民自備的木杆長槊與角弓。起義一方則是濟北郡內的逃戶、匿丁、逃兵、匠役與失去土地的農夫，因同鄉同里的關係結成的武裝，首領孟海公自號「黑社帥」，眾至數萬。「黑社」之名，舊說以為是取黑布為幟、以黑巾裹頭為號的民間結社，諸說並存，文獻未詳；可以確定的是起義者並非單一隊伍，而是同一郡內數股勢力合流而成，彼此沒有編制，除了首領之外也不存在共同的上級。部眾沒有固定營區與後方，作戰靠剽掠郡縣、截取官倉、收編逃卒就地取給。這種武裝與河北山東其他起義——張金稱、孫安祖、高士達、竇建德——在同一條線上互相呼應，也互相爭奪糧源與地盤，使隋廷無法集中兵力逐次平定。
countriesEn: The two sides were the Sui state apparatus in the neighbourhood of Jibei Commandery in Shandong on one hand, and on the other the village armed bands mustered by Meng Haigong under the name Black Standard Leader. On the Sui side, every unit that could really fight was far away in the north: the second campaign against Goguryeo had taken the capital's household guard, the picked troops of Guanzhong and the transport labour of the river routes, so that what remained in the central plain were the commandery and county levies enrolled on the spot; they were armed and drilled while the disturbance lasted, held the walls in ranks, and returned to the fields afterwards. The only force able to pursue was a handful of cavalry columns brought back from the front or hastily recruited, led by experienced commanders and sent county by county to hunt the rebels down. Yanggu, the seat of Jibei Commandery, belonged to Qizhou; the ordinary duties of the county levies there were to hold the city, to seize absentees and to supervise the dikes, their man strength came from the registered households, and their weapons were mostly wooden-shafted spears and horn bows provided by the villages themselves. The insurgents were fugitives from the household registers, concealed persons, deserters, craftsmen and landless peasants from within Jibei, banded together through the ties of village and neighbourhood; their leader Meng Haigong styled himself Black Standard Leader, and his numbers are given as reaching tens of thousands. The name Black Society is commonly taken to refer to a popular association with black banners and black headcloths, but the accounts vary and the literature does not settle it; what can be said is that the rising was not a single force but the confluence of several bands in one commandery, without establishment and, apart from the leader, without any common superior. The bands had no fixed canton and no rear; they lived by raiding commanderies, seizing official granaries and taking in deserters, and they drew their supplies on the spot. Such armed groups answered to the other risings in Hebei and Shandong — Zhang Jincheng, Sun Anzu, Gao Shida, Dou Jiande — along the same lines, and competed with them for grain and ground, so that the court could never concentrate its troops to suppress them one after another.
people: 孟海公是這場起義唯一留下姓名的首領。他是濟北郡人，郡治陽谷，即今山東聊城一帶；大業九年聚眾起兵，自稱黑社帥。除此之外，籍貫、出身、年齡、起兵的具體日期以及兵敗後的下落，諸史皆無記載，連一次兩軍交戰的過程也沒有留下來。隋廷方面的關鍵人物在中央：煬帝坐鎮涿郡，經營遼東第二次征高句麗，天下精兵與糧運都在那一線，山東各郡無力可恃，只能分遣將領逐處應變；樊子蓋在東都主持討逆，以刑峻著名，屬下稍有違令即加斬決；張須陀是這一年在河北山東追討群盜最有名的一員宿將，他以精騎先擊其眾、再追奔潰散之師，接連破張金稱、高士達、孫安祖諸部，高士達的部眾潰散之後多歸田里。九月，楊玄感在黎陽起兵響應，眾至約八萬，兵敗之後河北的官軍調度為之一空，濟北一線的郡兵更難集中，這正是同年河北起義此起彼伏的關鍵節點。河北另一支更強大的武裝是竇建德，他的眾後來達到數十萬，並與孟海公一類的起義遙相呼應；孟海公失敗之後，部分部眾流入竇建德、張金稱的軍中，成為大業十年以後河北割據的兵源之一。
peopleEn: Meng Haigong is the only leader of this rising whose name survives. He was a man of Jibei Commandery, whose seat was Yanggu, in the region of modern Liaocheng in Shandong; he mustered a following and rose in arms in the ninth year of Daye, styling himself Black Standard Leader. Beyond that, his native place within the commandery, his background, his age, the exact date on which he raised his banner and what became of him after his defeat are all absent from the histories; not even the account of a single engagement between the two sides has come down to us. On the court side the decisive figures were at the centre. Emperor Yang sat at Zhuojun running the second Goguryeo campaign in Liaodong, with the picked troops and the grain traffic of the whole country tied up on that front, so the commanderies of Shandong had nothing to rely on and could only dispatch commanders piecemeal to deal with each outbreak. Fan Zigae directed the suppression from the Eastern Capital and was famous for severity, having subordinates executed for the slightest breach of orders. Zhang Xuotuo was the best known of the veteran commanders chasing the bands in Hebei and Shandong that year; he struck the mass of the insurgents with cavalry first and then pursued the broken host into the roads, breaking Zhang Jincheng, Gao Shida and Sun Anzu in turn, and the followers of Gao Shida dispersed to their fields once they were broken. In the ninth month Yang Xiangan rose at Liyang in answer, gathering about eighty thousand men, and the dispersal of his host after his defeat left the imperial disposition in Hebei empty, so that the levies of the Jibei line could no longer be concentrated; that was the critical hinge of the risings that followed one another in Hebei that year. The other and far greater armed body in Hebei was Dou Jiande, whose following later reached tens of thousands and who answered Meng Haigong's kind of rising from a distance. After Meng Haigong's failure part of his men flowed into the hosts of Dou Jiande and Zhang Jincheng and became one of the sources of man power for the Hebei powers after the tenth year of Daye.
kits: 卡面這件羅馬方陣盾（scutum）出現在共和末期到帝政前期的義大利：高約一公尺、寬約六七十公分，長方形而略作凸面，木胎蒙皮、邊緣包鐵，中央鑄有盾鈕，是重裝步兵劍士與早期密集盾陣步兵的標準防具。Polybius 所記載的羅馬軍陣，前排三列密集而盾緣彼此咬合，盾牌不靠厚度取勝，靠的是整列合成一面連續的弧形障壁；卡面那句「羅馬的防線靠盾緣咬住盾緣」說的就是這件事。這套技術源自希臘世界與伊利里亞工匠的血脈，在東亞從未出現。613年的山東鄉里起義與羅馬沒有任何瓜葛，東亞同時期與之最接近的形制反而是方盾：漢代出土的漆盾、彩繪盾即是方形木胎蒙革，隋唐之間盾的形制分圓、方兩式，隋軍步卒用盾遮蔽身體、與長槊配合結陣，攻城則用櫓與撞車。隋代軍器的主幹是長槊、環首刀與弓弩：長槊是步卒的基本兵器，用於結陣拒馬；弓弩以角筋複合弓、蹶張弩、機弩與床弩為主，床弩一發重箭可破門；防具有札甲、兜鍪、鐵鍔與盾，騎兵另有頸甲與馬鎧；輔助器械有撞車、雲梯、拒馬、鹿角，並用火矢與猛火油對付城牆與船隊。起義的一端幾乎沒有像樣的防具：兵器是竹木削成的槊、柴刀改成的長刀、戈、獵弓，以及耒耜、漁叉一類削尖的農具漁具，鎧甲極少，盾更難得，因為鄉里武裝帶不走多少笨重的木胎。孟海公這類黑社眾的旗幟與標記，史料沒有留下記載；可以確定的是他們靠人數與對鄉里道路的熟悉取勝，靠的是人，不是裝備。
kitsEn: The Roman scutum on the card belongs to Italy of the late Republic and the early Principate. It stood about a metre high and sixty to seventy centimetres wide, rectangular and slightly convex, of a wooden core covered with hide, edged with iron and fitted with a metal boss at the centre; it was the standard protection of the armoured swordsmen and of the infantry of the early dense shield formations. In the battle order described by Polybius, the first three lines stood shoulder to shoulder with the rims of their shields locked to one another, and the shield won no victory by thickness but by a whole rank combining into a continuous curved wall; the sentence on the card, that the Roman line held by the rim biting the rim rather than by the thickness of the shield, names exactly this. The craft behind it descends from the Greek world and from Illyrian workmanship, and it never reached East Asia. The village rising of 613 in Shandong has nothing whatever to do with Rome, and the form in East Asia closest to it was in fact the square shield: the lacquered and painted shields excavated from Han tombs are square wooden cores covered with hide, and between Sui and Tang the shield came in round and square forms, the Sui foot soldier using the shield to cover the body and to fight in line with the long shao, while siege work relied on the movable screen and the battering ram. The trunk of Sui armaments was the long shao, the ring-pommel dao and the bow and crossbow: the long shao was the basic arm of the foot soldier, used to form a bristling line; the bows and crossbows were the composite bow of horn and sinew, the strong-pull crossbow, the light crossbow and the bed crossbow, and a single heavy bolt from the bed crossbow could break a gate. Armour was lamellar plate, iron helms, iron-edged shields and blade guards, the cavalry adding neck guards and horse armour; field and siege adjuncts included battering rams, scaling ladders, cheval-de-frise and antler-shaped obstacles, and fire arrows and naphtha were used against walls and ships. At the other end of the field there was almost no protection worth the name: the weapons were bamboo and wooden shao, long knives reworked from billhooks, the ge, hunting bows, and farming and fishing implements sharpened into points, for armour was scarce and shields harder still, since a village band could not carry away many heavy wooden cores. The banners and marks of the Black Society followers such as Meng Haigong are not recorded in the sources; what can be said is that they won by numbers and by knowing the roads of their own countryside, and that their strength was men rather than equipment.
tactics: 鄉里起義的戰術基因是不據大城、不結硬陣、不與官軍主力正面合戰。孟海公這類首領手上的部眾，多數只靠同鄉關係維繫，沒有操練、沒有攻城器械，最常見的打法是先以小股人馬在郡城之外的鄉里活動，避開郡兵主力，等守軍出城或被調往別處，再合擊縣邑、截斷糧道；奪得倉廩之後把糧食分給部眾，趁著隋軍主力遠在遼東、郡兵被四面的起義拖住的時間窗口擴張。一旦精騎到達，起義者便放棄城池，退入鄉里、澤地與水網地帶，用地形切割追兵縱隊，再在夜間或雨霧中襲擊糧隊與傳令兵。攻城沒有器械便靠突門、攀牆與火攻：拆民舍取梁木作撞杆、用浸油麻布焚燒城門、拆屋瓦投擲守軍；更多時候不攻城，只破外郭、掠府庫與鹽場。隋軍這邊的戰術相對規整：郡兵與縣兵據城固守，閉門拒敵，以弩矢、拒馬與礟石守城頭，決不輕出；追討軍的辦法是先以精騎衝擊起義者的散眾，再追潰散之師，迫其在道路上疲於奔命，同時修築營柵、封鎖道路、斷其汲道與糧道，讓起義者得不到食宿與補充。合圍之後，郡兵與追討軍會合，以「討」為名誘敵出戰，一鼓而潰。這類衝突通常沒有會戰的名分，勝負在數日之內以眾散、渠帥被擒收場。
tacticsEn: The tactical inheritance of a village rising was: do not hold a great city, do not form a hard line, do not meet the imperial main force in a set-piece battle. The followers of a leader such as Meng Haigong were held together only by village acquaintance, without drill and without siege equipment, so the usual method was to move in small parties outside the commandery seat, avoid the county levies, and wait for the garrison to march out or to be drawn off elsewhere before striking the county towns together and cutting the grain road. Once a granary was taken, the grain was shared out among the band, and the rising grew inside the window in which the imperial main force was still in Liaodong and the county levies were being drawn this way and that by risings on every side. Once the cavalry arrived, the insurgents would leave the towns, fall back into the countryside, the marsh country and the water network, use the ground to cut the columns of pursuit, and raid baggage trains and couriers by night or in rain and mist. Without siege engines the taking of a town was done by surprising the gate, scaling the wall and by fire: beams pulled out of houses to serve as rams, oil-soaked sacking set against the gates, roof tiles thrown down on the defenders. More often they did not assault the city at all, but broke the outer enclosure and took the treasury offices and the salt pans. On the Sui side the method was more regular. Commandery and county levies held their towns, kept the gates shut against the enemy, met them with crossbow bolts, cheval-de-frise and stones from the ramparts, and did not venture out. The pursuing columns struck the scattered insurgents with cavalry first and then chased the broken host, wearing them out on the roads, while at the same time building fortified camps, sealing the roads and closing their springs and their grain roads so that the insurgents could find neither food nor shelter. Once the net was closed, the levies and the pursuing cavalry joined, called the enemy out under the pretext of giving battle, and broke them in a single charge. A conflict of this kind usually had no battle to be named; it was settled within days by the dispersal of the band or the capture of its commander.
data: 可核的數字多來自編年史對大業九年全局的記載，而非這場起義本身。兵員方面，《資治通鑑》記隋軍第二次征高句麗渡遼之師號一百一十三萬五千人，而糧運不繼，至遼東時士卒死者過半；正是這一支遠在東北的隊伍，掏空了山東各郡可以倚仗的兵源。起義的規模，編年只說孟海公眾至數萬，這是史書所記的上限，也是當時群盜習用的誇大說法；起義既限於濟北一郡，能列為戰鬥力的數目當在數千至數萬之間，既無更細記載，也不宜作更精確的推斷。河北同期起義的數字可以作為尺度：張金稱在鄴郡聚眾號稱百萬，竇建德眾至數十萬，九月楊玄感在黎陽起兵聚眾約八萬，而張須陀破高士達時斬首萬餘級、俘虜數萬，其眾隨即散歸田里。糧食與物資方面，《隋書》記大業九年江南、江淮大水，漕渠與堤壩受損，前線給養中斷，河北、山東同時乏食；二月朝廷下詔括天下漏丁，把逃戶、匿丁與度人為僧道者一律重新登記以充軍實與租調，郡縣為完成額外額數而四處追捕人戶，民間因而群起。距離與時間上，濟北郡治陽谷距京師洛陽約六百里、距涿郡約七百里，郡兵自州城調到屬縣多需數日，山東各郡的兵力無法在數日之內集中到同一方向，這正是起義得以蔓延的實際原因。
dataEn: The figures that can be checked come mostly from the annalistic account of the situation in the ninth year of Daye, and not from this rising itself. On numbers of troops, the Zizhi Tongjian records that the Sui army crossing to Liaodong for the second campaign against Goguryeo was numbered at one million one hundred and thirty-five thousand men, and that because supply did not keep up, more than half the soldiers were dead by the time they reached Liaodong; that distant army in the northeast was precisely what hollowed out the man power the commanderies of Shandong could rely on. As for the size of the rising, the annals say only that Meng Haigong's following reached tens of thousands, which is the ceiling the histories give and also the standard exaggeration of the bands of that age. Since the rising was confined to a single commandery, the number that could be put in the line must have lain between a few thousand and a few tens of thousands; there is no finer record, and no more exact inference is warranted. The figures for the risings in Hebei in the same year give a scale: Zhang Jincheng claimed a hundred thousand at Ye, Dou Jiande's following reached tens of thousands, and in the ninth month Yang Xiangan assembled about eighty thousand men at Liyang, while when Zhang Xuotuo broke Gao Shida he took more than ten thousand heads and tens of thousands of prisoners, and the host then dispersed back to the fields. On grain and supplies, the History of Sui records great floods in Jiangnan and the Jiang-Huai in the ninth year of Daye, the canal and the embankments damaged and the supply of the front cut off, while Hebei and Shandong were short of food at the same time; in the second month the court ordered a general registration of all hidden persons, so that absentees, concealed households and those who had taken monastic vows might be entered anew as liable for service and for tax, and the counties hunted from house to house to produce the extra quotas, which is why the villages rose. On distance and time, Yanggu, the seat of Jibei Commandery, lay some six hundred li from the capital of Luoyang and some seven hundred li from Zhuojun, county levies needed several days to move from the prefectural seat down to the county seats, and the troops of the Shandong commanderies could not be brought together in the same direction within a few days, which is the practical reason the rising was able to spread.
cause: 大業九年之所以會有這樣一場起義，緣由是多層的。最直接的一層是括戶：二月朝廷下詔清查天下漏丁，逃戶、匿丁與度人為僧道者一律重新登記，任何人不得隱匿，州縣官吏為完成額外的丁口與租調額數，挨家挨戶追人，鄉里之間互相舉發，怨憤集中在同一時刻爆發。第二層是戰爭的抽空：第二次征高句麗把國家的兵源、馬匹、器械與漕運全部調到北方，前線在江淮水災、漕渠受損之後缺糧，而山東各郡能出兵的只剩就地抽丁的郡兵，防守出現空隙。第三層是饑荒與兼併：大業九年江南、江淮大水，河北山東亦乏食，豪右兼併土地、官府卻只知催斂，失了田地的人無以為生，於是脫離編戶，成為流民與亡命。第四層是治理的嚴苛與失控：樊子蓋在東都以刑峻著稱，各郡縣的胥吏與將校對逃亡戶的追捕常常越出常度，百姓與官府的對立被推到不能再緩的地步。在這樣的環境裏，任何一個能號召人的首領都可能在旬日之間聚起數萬之眾；起義本身多數沒有綱領與政權形式，跑到一起的是「社」——一種鄉里之間的互助與秘密色彩兼具的結社，隋末唐初民間彌勒信仰的傳播與此同時興，各地名號不一，諸說並存，但可以確定的是，「社」的名目讓互不相識的鄉民有了最初的組織形式。
causeEn: The reasons behind such a rising in the ninth year of Daye lay in several layers. The most immediate was the general registration of the population: in the second month the court ordered a search for all hidden persons throughout the empire, so that absentees, concealed households and those who had taken monastic vows were entered anew, and nobody was allowed to hide; the county officials, pressed to produce the extra numbers of liable persons and of tax, hunted from house to house, villages informed on one another, and the accumulated resentment burst out at a single moment. The second layer was the emptying of the country by the war: the second Goguryeo campaign drew the state's manpower, horses, equipment and river transport to the north, and once the floods in the Jiang-Huai broke the canal the front went short of food, while all the Shandong commanderies could put into the field were the levies enrolled on the spot, leaving a gap in the defence. The third layer was famine and annexation of land: in the ninth year of Daye Jiangnan and the Jiang-Huai were drowned, Hebei and Shandong were short of food, the powerful annexed the fields while the officials did nothing but press for payment, and men who had lost their land had no way to live, so they fell out of the registers and became vagrants and fugitives. The fourth layer was the harshness and loss of control of the administration: Fan Zigae was famous for severity at the Eastern Capital, and in the counties and commanderies the clerks and officers who chased absentees often went beyond all bounds, until the antagonism between the people and the government could no longer be held back. In such a setting any leader able to call men could raise tens of thousands within a fortnight. The risings themselves mostly had no programme and no form of government; what brought them together was the society, an association combining neighbourhood mutual aid with a colouring of secrecy. The spread of popular Maitreya belief in the late Sui and early Tang belonged to the same time, the names differed from place to place and the accounts vary, but what can be certain is that the name of the society gave village men with no prior acquaintance a first form of organisation.
impact: 單看孟海公這一場，史料只留下一個名字與一個號，它帶來的直接改變有限：濟北一郡的統治秩序被打斷數月，縣吏與里正的權威失效，郡兵與郡倉的控制在鄉里一段時間內名存實亡，之後仍回到州府的管治之下。但放進大業九年整體看，這類州郡起義構成了一條清楚的連鎖：它們把隋朝最後的財政與兵源基礎，也就是編戶齊民與租調力役，從內部挖空，使朝廷對地方的抽汲愈來愈急，而地方愈來愈不能提供，兩者互為因果。河北、山東因此不能穩定地供應兵員與糧食，遼東的戰事就再也沒有可持續的物資支撐。示範作用同樣重要：鄉里武裝證明了只要官軍主力被牽制在外，州城是可以被拿下的，倉廩是可以被分的；同一條邏輯，後來被瓦崗軍在黎陽倉、李密在洛陽、竇建德在漳南一一重演。大業十年以後河北的郡縣多歸竇建德、劉黑闕、王世充等武裝，隋朝在名義上還有天下，能調動的郡兵卻所剩無幾。對後世史書編纂而言，有姓名而無事跡本身也是一種記錄：唐初修《隋書》，把關於這些小股起義的零星材料收進帝紀的編年目錄，卻不為他們立傳，使這批人在文獻中的存在感遠低於其當時的破壞力。
impactEn: Taken alone, the rising of Meng Haigong left behind a name and a title and changed little directly: the order of a single commandery was broken for some months, the authority of the county clerks and village headmen lapsed, the control of the levies and the granaries existed in name only for a time, and afterwards everything went back under the government of the prefecture. Set within the ninth year of Daye as a whole, however, these county risings formed a clear chain. They hollowed out from within the last financial and manpower base of the Sui, the registered taxed households and the rent and labour services, so that the extraction by the court grew ever heavier while the localities grew ever less able to provide, each feeding the other. Hebei and Shandong could no longer supply soldiers and grain with any steadiness, and the war in Liaodong was never again to have a sustainable material support behind it. The demonstration was just as important. Armed bands built on village loyalty proved that, as long as the imperial main force was tied down elsewhere, a prefectural city could be taken and a granary could be divided; the same logic was played out afterwards by the Wagang host at the Liyang granary, by Li Mi at Luoyang and by Dou Jiande at Zhangnan. After the tenth year of Daye the commanderies of Hebei were mostly in the hands of armed bodies such as Dou Jiande, Liu Hei and Wang Shichong; the Sui still claimed the empire on paper while the county levies it could actually move were almost gone. For the writing of later history, too, a name without a career is itself a kind of record: when the Tang compiled the History of Sui, the scattered materials on these small risings went into the annalistic roster of the emperor's reign and no biography was written for them, so that their presence in the written record is far smaller than the disruption they actually caused.
result: 結局是這場起義沒有發展成可以自立的一方，也沒有留下可供追認的會戰記錄。官軍的處置方式與同年其他州郡起義相同：郡兵與縣兵先封守住縣境要道，調回前線或臨時募得的精騎入境，以追討潰散之師的方式迫使起義者分散，孟海公的部眾在失去郡城、倉廩與同鄉網絡之後各自散去，其中一部分併入竇建德、張金稱的軍隊，成為大業十年前後河北與山東義軍的兵源；首領孟海公本人的下落，編年史並無記載，後世也沒有留下任何傳記，這正是隋末數百名起義首領中相當一部分的共同命運。放到全局看，大業九年爆發的起義潮在大約一年之內被隋廷以郡兵、募兵與鎮守重鎮的策略逐一壓下去，但每一次鎮壓都消耗掉一批可用之兵與一筆可收之賦，而新的叛亂總在別的州郡重新冒出來，隋朝的崩解因此不是由某一次戰役決定，而是被這條不斷重複的循環耗盡。三年之後，大業十三年（617）太原留守李淵起兵；再一年，隋煬帝在江都遇弒，隋朝覆亡，唐朝接手的地方秩序，是在這批起義已經把郡縣系統打散之後重新拼起來的。
resultEn: The outcome was that the rising never developed into a power able to stand on its own, and it left no engagement that could afterwards be commemorated. The treatment on the imperial side was the same as for the other county risings of that year: county levies first sealed the roads into the districts, cavalry brought back from the front or hastily recruited entered the country, and the insurgents were scattered by the pursuit of their broken host. Meng Haigong's followers, once they had lost the commandery seat, the granaries and the network of village acquaintance, dispersed of their own accord, and part of them was absorbed into the hosts of Dou Jiande and Zhang Jincheng, becoming man power for the insurgents of Hebei and Shandong around the tenth year of Daye. The fate of Meng Haigong himself is not recorded in the annals and no biography of him survives, which was the common lot of a good many hundreds of rebel leaders at the end of the Sui. Across the whole picture, the wave of risings that broke out in the ninth year of Daye was put down one by one within roughly a year, by county levies, recruits and the strategy of holding strategic towns, but every suppression consumed a batch of usable soldiers and a sum of collectable revenue, and a new rebellion always surfaced in some other commandery. The collapse of the Sui was therefore not decided by any single battle; it was exhausted by this constantly repeated cycle. Three years later, in the thirteenth year of Daye (617), the Taiyuan garrison commander Li Yuan rose in arms; a year after that the emperor was killed at Jiangdu and the Sui fell. The local order that the Tang took over was reassembled out of the pieces which these risings had already broken apart.
